highlights.title: Apple TV’s great year continues with Small Prophets
highlights.summary: Apple TV has had a really great run in 2026 - and a cozy new addition is helping expand its lineup even more. As the streaming service has attempted to grow in order to better compete with the likes of Disney and Netflix, it has steadily broadened the range of its series.
body: A quirky supernatural comedy is the latest welcome addition to the streaming service.

Then one day his dad has an idea: He tells Michael a secret, alchemical recipe that will let him grow tiny magical beings that can answer any question. And since Michael is desperate to know the answer to one particular question — will he ever see Clea again? — he decides to try it, despite not really believing it will work.

What follows is chaotically comical. Michael ends up partnering with his curious coworker Kacey (Lauren Patel) to grow the creatures, called homunculi, but at the same time his previously simple life becomes much more complex. Michael’s father keeps getting into trouble at his nursing home, his neighbors keep threatening to call the council because of his messy yard, and Clea’s broke brother Roy (Paul Kaye) is trying to claim the house so he can sell it and get out of debt. All the while, the homunculi are growing in both size and power.
points: Apple TV has had a really great run in 2026 - and a cozy new addition is helping expand its lineup even more.
As the streaming service has attempted to grow in order to better compete with the likes of Disney and Netflix, it has steadily broadened the range of its series.

highlights.title: Chris Bourg named vice provost and Barbara K. Ostrom (1978) Director of the MIT Libraries
highlights.summary: Chris Bourg, who has served as director of the MIT Libraries since 2015, has been named vice provost and Barbara K. Ostrom (1978) Director of the Libraries, MIT Provost Anantha Chandrakasan announced today.
body: “The title ‘vice provost’ signals the enduring importance of the MIT Libraries in the digital age,” said Chandrakasan. “While the ways in which the libraries meet the needs of our community might change as technology changes, their mission of protecting access to knowledge and information is as vital as ever.”

Thanks to a generous gift from Barbara K. Ostrom ’78, SM ’78, the position of the director of the libraries now has an endowment to help fund it in perpetuity. Bourg noted that the gift is especially meaningful for her, due to the sense of service she shares with Ostrom: they both completed Reserve Officers' Training Corps (ROTC) during their time as undergraduates — Bourg at Duke University and Ostrom at MIT — before going on to active military service.

highlights.title: Was it right to default Medvedev for hitting spectator with ball?
highlights.summary: Daniil Medvedev was defaulted for hitting a spectator with the ball during his semi-final with Novak Djokovic at the China Open, but was it the correct decision or should he have been able to continue playing?
body: Medvedev was trailing Djokovic 7-5 5-3 and had lost a point when he hit the ball coming off the wall.
The spectator, who was ​sitting in the first row behind Medvedev, clutched his left eye and appeared to ‌be in pain as he walked out of the gallery, assisted by stadium staff.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Jonathan Overend said: "From the first camera angle we saw the ball leaving Medvedev's racket and weren't sure where it had gone, but I later saw a different angle filmed from the stands and it clearly went straight from the racket into the face of this spectator and so from the minute that was obvious, it was an instant default.

"It was absolutely the correct decision. The rulebook is very clear about that and it was unfortunate for Medvedev. We take him at face value when he says he didn't mean to do it, but it did leave his racket with force and it did strike the spectator.

highlights.title: ‘We live in grief-phobic societies’: experts on how to get more comfortable with death
highlights.summary: We are all going to die, and so is everyone we know. So how can you not be terrified? For most people, death is not a standard conversation topic. Once, at lunch, a friend began talking about her mother’s death several years earlier.
body: Afterwards, I asked him what was wrong. “I really don’t like talking about death,” he said, his hands twitching anxiously. “I don’t even like thinking about it. It freaks me out.”
His discomfort struck me as silly – and also the most normal thing in the world. We are all going to die, and so is everyone we know. So why be terrified? And how can you not be terrified?

My friend is far from alone in his discomfort. “We live in grief-illiterate and grief-phobic societies,” says Dr Lucy Hone, a resilience and grief researcher and author of the book How Will I Get Ever Through This?: A Practical Guide to Navigating Life’s Toughest Times.

Hone began researching grief over a decade ago, after the sudden death of her daughter, Abi. On our video call, she wears one of Abi’s old hats, an orange and white beanie with polka dots and a big orange pouf on top. It’s ridiculous, Hone says, but it makes her laugh.

highlights.title: We can’t just change the definition of ‘recording’
highlights.summary: With AI hardware, tech companies are pushing the definition of what does and doesn't constitute a recording. For most of gadget history, it'd be reasonable to assume that a device with a microphone or camera is either recording you or it isn't; it's either on or off, without much gray area.
body: Tech companies with new AI hardware want you to agree that always-listening, often-recapping devices don’t count as recording.

Last week, Bloomberg ’s Mark Gurman reported that Apple is working on a smart home camera that doesn’t save video recordings. Instead, AI uses the visual data to create text snippets that describe what’s happening around your home. Supposedly, it’ll support facial recognition, but without video footage. The idea is that it still protects some privacy. This tech, Gurman says, is similar to how the cameras in rumored future AirPods will also work.

It’s similar to Apple’s Audio Intelligence on the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4. The Apple Watch has had a microphone for ages, mostly for Siri and taking phone calls from the wrist. Of the four Audio Intelligence features, two have caused the most debate online: Live Rewind and Siri Recap. The former produces a transcript of the past 15 seconds, whereas the latter can generate high-level summaries of the conversations you have throughout the day.
points: With AI hardware, tech companies are pushing the definition of what does and doesn't constitute a recording.
For most of gadget history, it'd be reasonable to assume that a device with a microphone or camera is either recording you or it isn't; it's either on or off, without much gray area.

highlights.title: UEFA monitoring Man City case as it considers potential action
highlights.summary: UEFA is monitoring developments and will wait until the end of the Premier League's disciplinary process before deciding whether to take any potential action against Manchester City.
body: City have been found guilty by an independent commission of breaking the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018, including five charges of failing to comply with UEFA's Financial Fair Play rules.
UEFA financial rules at the time meant clubs were effectively limited to spending what they earned within set break-even requirements.
The independent commission found that City's owners put in £830m of their own money and disguised it as sponsorship income for nine seasons.
City are appealing against the decision and maintain they have a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence which will clear their name.

highlights.title: Tom Cruise Said He Doesn’t Make Movies for ‘Opening Weekend’ Right Before ‘Digger’ Bombed: ‘You Hope to Make a Film That Can Last’
highlights.summary: Tom Cruise suffered one of his worst box office openings in history with “Digger,” Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s satirical black comedy that bombed with $8 million in North America on a production budget north of $160 million. But Cruise isn’t one to judge a movie based on its first weekend in theaters.
body: “They transcend… you just hope you can make a film that can last,” Cruise said. “So many things happen when you open a movie. I was fortunate to release movies in the 80s and 90s, when movies would stay in the theater for a year. With ‘Rain Man’ and ‘Born on the Fourth of July,’ these movie would just play and play for a year. How can I make a film that can translate and last and evolve? And I feel that way…. that is ‘Digger,’ it’s one of those movies.”

With its production budget between $160 million and $180 million, plus a $100 million marketing budget, “Digger” would need to gross $350 million in theaters worldwide just to break even at the box office. That figure will be impossible to hit after the movie’s $20 million global start. The movie is now primed to lose at least $150 million to $200 million theatrically.

highlights.title: Atlassian and OpenAI expand partnership to turn enterprise knowledge into action
highlights.summary: Atlassian and OpenAI are expanding their partnership to connect frontier models with enterprise knowledge and help teams plan, build, and deliver work.
body: Atlassian and OpenAI are expanding their partnership, bringing frontier models in the GPT‑6 family across Atlassian’s platform to power AI experiences that help teams plan, build, and deliver work. The combination of both companies’ capabilities will give joint customers more ways to work with Atlassian products and OpenAI.

Under a new agreement, OpenAI frontier models will power agents across Atlassian’s platform and Rovo. Rovo combines OpenAI intelligence with Atlassian’s Teamwork Graph, an enterprise context layer that connects people, projects, documents, and decisions, giving AI a deep understanding of how a company works.

The expanded partnership builds on a collaboration that began in 2023 and arrives as Atlassian broadens its own adoption of Codex and ChatGPT Enterprise. More than 3,000 Atlassian developers use Codex across their terminals, IDEs, and code review workflows. Through Atlassian plugins powered by the Teamwork Graph, Codex users can access relevant work items and technical documentation, helping developers write, test, and ship software.

highlights.title: Neutrino physicist wins 2026 Nobel Physics Prize
highlights.summary: Francis Halzen, a physicist at the University of Wisconsin, Madison, has won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics "for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.” Halzen spearheaded the development and construction of…
body: “It was a great surprise, and I obviously didn’t expect it,” Halzen said during a news conference in Stockholm, Sweden, speaking by phone from Italy. While the Nobel was awarded to Halzen, he emphasized that his work was the result of a “large collaboration” with other researchers.

“This reflects on the really courageous people who joined me in this project when really no respectable conservative physicist would have joined me. But many talented people did, and that’s why I’m here,” he said.

“I am shocked and absolutely delighted that Francis was awarded the Nobel this year,” said particle physicist Danielle Norcini of Johns Hopkins University in a statement. “He is the scientific visionary and driving force behind [IceCube]. It has transformed our understanding of the universe by detecting the first high-energy neutrinos from beyond our galaxy, opening an entirely new field of neutrino astronomy. The experiment is the extraordinary achievement of hundreds of scientists, engineers, and collaborators, but Francis was the person who dreamed big enough to imagine an experiment of this scale and then relentlessly pushed to make it a reality.”

highlights.title: USA will be 'underdogs' in 2027 Ryder Cup - Furyk
highlights.summary: United States Ryder Cup captain Jim Furyk says his team will be "underdogs" when they attempt to end more than 30 years of pain on European soil in next year's edition at Adare Manor.
body: United States captain Jim Furyk says his team will be "underdogs" when they attempt to end more than 30 years of pain on European soil in next year's Ryder Cup at Adare Manor.
The Americans have not claimed an away Ryder Cup victory since 1993, losing all seven contests in Europe since that victory at The Belfry.

Furyk, who oversaw a 17½-10½ loss to Europe in France in 2018, was handed a second stint as captain earlier this year following Keegan Bradley's team's defeat to Luke Donald's Europe at Bethpage Black in 2025.

"We know what we are up against, we also know it's been 34 years since we won in Europe. There is no secret, I'm going to hear it over and over again so I am going to embrace it," Furyk said during a news conference at Adare Manor in County Limerick.

There are two ways to redeem promo codes in Escape From Tarkov. The first is to boot up the game launcher, then click on the drop-down arrow beneath your username in the top right-hand corner. Then select activate code and type in any of the codes listed above. If successful, you'll see green text telling you the reward has been claimed.

Alternatively, you can visit the official Escape From Tarkov promo code page on the website and type in the code there. Make sure you're signed in when you do so, and if you play Tarkov through Steam, ensure your account is linked.

When redeemed, go in-game and click on the messenger tab at the bottom of the screen. You'll find your rewards for each code by selecting "get" on all the messages. If you don't have the stash space for all of it, don't fret: you can come back and retrieve the rest of the rewards later on.

highlights.title: Googlebook "Better Together" phone features don't work with Samsung at launch
highlights.summary: Googlebooks are Google's latest attempt to carve out a piece of the premium laptop market, and tight integration with Android phones is a key part of that effort. Now that Googlebooks are available, we're learning of some frustrating limitations of that plan.
body: When Google announced the launch window for Googlebooks, it said the laptops were "engineered to work with your Android phone right out of the box." But as with many things Google, the truth is more convoluted. We have since learned that you need Android 17 for any of the nifty integrations to work. With a compatible Android 17 phone, you can seamlessly stream apps to your laptop, access files on your phone, mirror notifications, and continue where you left off in certain apps when switching from phone to laptop.

You might think that the latest Samsung phones, which shipped with Android 17, would be ready for this experience. You'd be wrong, though. Some early Googlebook adopters have complained that phones like the Z Fold 8 won't work with the laptops. While the devices appear to see each other, the phone doesn't stay connected. Google representatives have since confirmed that these "Better Together" features are not currently supported on even the latest Samsung phones. An update that brings support to Samsung phones will roll out in "the coming weeks."

body: The technical ability throughout the world-class squad Arsenal have assembled could hardly be higher but the levels of grit, resilience and tenacity need examining in a group that appear unable to match Chelsea and Manchester City when it comes to the mental aspects of a title race. Arsenal last won the WSL in 2019.

When speaking to sources close to the Arsenal players, it is common to hear of the squad being like a “family”, very supportive of each other and full of “great people”. Those admirable traits, and a general sense the club is full of nice characters, often come across when watching games or during player interviews. Arsenal have built a team of good eggs; polite, courteous and professional individuals who people would be glad to call friends. In the vast majority of scenarios in life this is, quite obviously, a good thing. But are they too nice to beat City?

highlights.summary: OLED TVs are considered the best TVs for gaming. They're usually quite expensive, but Amazon is offering a fantastic deal on a Roku branded OLED TV during the October Prime Day Sale. For two days only, the 65" Roku Pro 4K OLED TV is available for $799.99 with free shipping.
body: The Roku Pro-series OLED TV was released. It's equipped with a 4K true W-OLED panel with a native 120Hz refresh rate and HDMI 2.1 inputs, making it an excellent TV for PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X console gaming. Although the Roku Pro isn't as expensive as other OLED TVs, it shares most of the advantages of its more expensive siblings, including the near instaneous response time, true black levels, near infinite contrast ratio, and ultra-wide viewing angles. It also has one nice feature that the rest don't have, and that's the Roku smart interface baked in.

I've tried every built-in smart interface extensively, and I consider Roku to be the best smart interface overall compared to other popular options like Google TV (Sony), Tizen (Samsung), WebOS (LG), or Fire TV (Panasonic). The Roku interface is easy to use, aesthetically pleasing, light on resources, and most importantly for me, it doesn't require you to commit to an ecosystem. Roku also has native compatibility with just about every streaming app out there.

highlights.title: Why is NASA bringing 7,500 contractors back to work as civil servants?
highlights.summary: As a flight director during NASA's Apollo missions, Gerry Griffin led several lunar landings. He helped bring the crew of Apollo 13 safely back to Earth. Later, he directed Johnson Space Center in Houston.
body: Through these experiences, Griffin learned the value of teamwork in spaceflight—during the dynamic moments that can make or break a successful launch or landing, you absolutely have to trust your colleagues in the trenches.

“When lightning struck the rocket during Apollo 12, we had to react in a hurry,” Griffin said in an interview. “With people like John Aaron and Jerry Carr, the trust and communications came through. It made the difference.”

This really happened in 1969. Griffin’s “Gold Team” in Mission Control led the launch of the Apollo 12 mission, when the ascending Saturn V rocket triggered lightning as it soared through electrically charged clouds. The lightning strike disrupted the Apollo spacecraft’s electrical systems, which flight controllers and astronaut Alan Bean scrambled to reset. The rocket and spacecraft survived, going on to complete the second lunar landing.

During the Apollo era, Griffin said, contractors were brought in to supplement NASA’s workforce. But the positions in Mission Control remained NASA employees, and that was important because the space agency ultimately had responsibility—success or failure—for what happened during its missions.

body: Hindi, Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu and Bangla-language titles are all part of the mix. The Malayalam catalog is especially deep, reflecting the weight of the region’s audience hailing from Kerala, where it is the dominant language.

Starzplay CEO Maaz Sheikh said that the region’s streamers will grow by pairing strong brands and giving viewers more for their money. “Audiences should not have to navigate an increasingly fragmented market to find the entertainment that matters to them. Bringing JioHotstar to Starzplay is a strategic investment in that future, combining the strength of India’s storytelling with our understanding of this region and the audiences we serve,” he said.

JioHotstar content is included in Starzplay’s Plus plan, which costs AED34.99 ($9.50) a month. The Max plan, at AED49.99 ($13.60) a month, pairs the full JioHotstar lineup with Starzplay’s sports rights, cricket among them. Starzplay positions itself as the region’s main destination for cricket.

highlights.title: The Tremendous Revival of Bangkok's Chao Phraya Waterfront
highlights.summary: Tony Perrottet visits the banks of the Chao Phraya River, where old-school noodle stalls now share space with Michelin-starred restaurants and gilded temples soar over former warehouses turned art galleries.
body: “I bought this boat to explore the river's hidden places,” said Jern, a Bangkok interior designer whose full name is Irinrat Prasongchaikul, as we chugged in her vintage cruiser across the terra-cotta-colored waters of the Chao Phraya River, or River of Kings. She had invited me to join her and a half-dozen local friends for a sunset spin on her romantic vessel, which was built in 1957 but whose polished-wood deck shaded by a canopy felt like a throwback to the colonial-era seafaring days of Joseph Conrad. The boatman soon steered us past the majestic Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn) to Thonburi, the less-frequented western side of the waterway, then navigated into a dreamy klong, or canal.
“I grew up in Bangkok knowing that the Chao Phraya was important,” Jern added, popping open an iced bottle of Champagne. “But there's so much that has been forgotten.”

Water in every form is revered in Thailand, Jern explained, and the Chao Phraya has special status. “As a Thai,” she said, “I was always taught to respect the water goddess, Phra Mae Khongkha, who is associated with purification and fertility. We are taught that we can live without electricity, but water is our first resource.”
